Method_Description: Individual data cells contain a flag if the concentration measured was (1) negative; (2) outside of the standard curve; or (3) below the limit of detection (LOD). The text flag is formatted as "[DataType]_[Below/Above]_[##]_ppm_[LOD/Standard]|[##]_ppm_Raw_Not_Corrected|[##]_ppm_Final_Corrected". The "|" is used to allow the user to parse apart the three pieces of information. The first part of the text string indicates the reason for the flag and the value of the LOD or Standard. The second part indicates the raw data value without any correction. The third part indicates the final corrected value. This value could be corrected based on dilution or other corrections (see the alphanumeric codes at the top of the data column for more details). A text string such as "NPOC_Above_30_ppm_Standard|30.1_ppm_Raw_Not_Corrected|415.2_ppm_Final_Corrected" indicates that the NPOC value is above the 30 parts per million (ppm) standard (the highest standard used); the raw value was 30.1ppm; and the corrected value (due to dilution) is 415.2ppm. The raw not corrected and final corrected values could be the same if there was no dilution or other corrections needed. Negative concentration values are not reported; rather "Negative_Value" and "-9999" are included in the text string (e.g. "NPOC_Below_0.5_ppm_LOD|Negative_Value_Raw_Not_Corrected|-9999_ppm_Final_Corrected"). For samples corrected to milligrams per kilogram values the raw data value without correction is the same as the raw milligrams per liter not corrected value.
Vials were intact and filled to appropriate levels.

Samples with "INC" in the sample name were kept in a temperature controlled chamber set at 21 degC before incubations. Following incubations, combined sediment and water samples were kept at room temperature. Samples with "SED" and "STR"  in the sample name were flash frozen and stored at -80 degC before extraction.
No additional preservation performed.

For samples with "INC" in the sample name, sediment was subsampled into pre-weighed 40 milliliter glass vial with an oxygen sensor spot. For samples with "SED" or "STR" in the sample name, sediment was subsampled into pre-weighed 50 milliliter proteomic friendly centrifuge tube.

For samples with "INC" in the sample name, the mass of the 40 milliliter glass vial and field moist sediment was recorded and a breathe-easy membrane was added to the vial opening. During incubation setup, 10 mL of sediment was added to each vial, and water was then added until there was no headspace in the 40 milliliter vial. For samples with "SED" in the sample name, the mass of a 50 milliliter proteomic friendly centrifuge tube was recorded and 10 grams of field moist sediment were added to the tube. Sediments were extracted with 20 milliliters of MilliQ water. For samples with "STR" in the sample name, the mass of a 50 milliliter proteomic friendly centrifuge tube was recorded; these samples were flash frozen and stored at -80 degreesC.

For samples with "INC", "SED" or "STR" in the sample name, dry sediment mass was calculated using site-specific average gravimetric moisture content (YEP1 vs YEP2). For INC samples, water mass was calculated as the water content in field moist sediment plus 30 grams, where 30 grams represents the calculated mass of water added during incubation setup (40 milliliters total vial volume - 10 milliliters sediment volume = 30 milliliters water, assuming water density of 1 grams_per_milliliters). For SED samples, water mass included field moist sediment water content plus 20 grams from MilliQ water used in the extraction. For STR samples, only field moist sediment water content was included. Sediment volume was only recorded for INC samples; SED and STR samples were assigned -9999 for this parameter.

Evacuated vials were purchased and filled with 20 mL of headspace equilibrated gas sample.
Samples stored upside down in 12 milliliter pre-evacuated gas sampling vials at room temperature.
No preservatives added.

20 mL of water sample was equlibrated with 20 mL of nitrogen gas by shaking gas/water mixture by hand for 2 minutes. 20 mL of the equlibrated gas sample was injected into the pre-evacuated 12 mL gas vial until the vial was overpressurized.

Gas samples were stored in 12 mL pre-evacuated gas vials and analyzed for the partial pressure of carbon dioxide (pCO2) and methane (pCH4) within two weeks after collection. Samples were analyzed for pCO2 and pCH4 in the laboratory using a Thermo Scientific Trace 1610 Gas Chromatograph equipped with a TriPlus RSH Smart autosampler and flame ionization detector, thermal conductivity detector, and electron capture detector detectors.

pCO2 and pCH4 values were corrected to account for dilution with nitrogen gas during headspace equilibration. Molar concentrations were then calculated based on the common gas law and Henry's law, adjusting for laboratory pressure and temperature during the incubations and the salinity of freshwaters (0.1 psu).

Vials were intact and filled to appropriate levels.
Upon field collection; wet and dry sediments were pre-incubated in a temperature controlled chamber set at 21 degC for 7 days prior to incubation.
Once every 24 hours the mass of the wet and dry sediments were recorded. Additional Milli-Q water was added to keep the mass of water consistent over the 7-day pre-incubation period.

24 hours before the incubation period, 10 milliliters of the wet and dry sediments were subsampled into 40 milliliter glass vials, covered with a Breatheasy membrane, and allowed to acclimate to the incubations chamber set to 21 degC. On the day of the incubation, synthetic river water (0 milligrams_C_per_liter), high severity Douglas-fir leachate (9 milligrams_C_per_liter) or unburned Douglas-fir leachate (9 milligrams_C_per_liter) was added to the corresponding treatment vials leaving no headspace. Firesting probes were inserted into the septa in the vial caps. The outside of the vial was sealed with Dow Corning high vacuum grease before the samples were placed on a Benchmark RotoBot Rotating Mixer set to 45 rpm which inverted the vials to 180 degrees, shaking for 3 seconds, before rotating 180 degrees back and shaking for 3 more seconds.
The DO was recorded every 5 seconds, and vials were left to incubate until DO reached below 2 milligrams per liter.

Respiration rates were calculated as the slope of the linear regression between dissolved oxygen (DO) measurements and incubation time. DO rates in milligrams DO per liter per hour were normalized to dry mass of sediment by multiplying by the liters of water in the incubation and dividing by the dry mass of sediment.
Samples were intact.
Sediments were immediately subsample upon field collection.
No preservatives added.
Tare weights for three drying tins (-1; -2; -3) were recorded before adding around 2 grams of homogenized sediment to each of the tared tins. Mass of the field moist sediment was recorded.

Sediment were dried at 105 degC for at least two days or until mass was stable. After drying samples were placed in a desiccator until cool. Mass of dried sediments plus the weighing vessel was recorded.
Gravimetric moisture was calculated as mass of field moist sediment minus mass of the dry sediment divided by the mass of the dry sediments.

Method_Description: Vials were intact and filled to appropriate levels.

Samples with OCN in the sample name: Filtered to 0.2 micrometers after incubation and stored at 4 degC in the dark until analysis. Samples with SOC in the sample name correspond to sediment extractions with MilliQ water. For these: sediments were stored at -80 degC before extraction. Water extracts were filtered to 0.2 micrometers and stored at 4 degC in the dark.
Samples with "OCN" or "SOC" in the name:  No preservatives added.

Samples with OCN in the sample name: After the incubation, the sample was filtered (0.2 micrometer Sterivex filter) into a polypropylene conical tube and stored until analysis. The samples were diluted with MilliQ water and transferred into analysis vial. Samples with SOC in the sample name correspond to sediment extractions with MilliQ water. 10 grams of sediment and 20 milliliters of Milli-Q water were added to a polypropylene conical tube; put on a shaker at 250 strokes per minute for 2 hours; and centrifuged at 6000 relative centrifugal force (rcf) for 5 minutes. The extracted supernatant was filtered (0.2 micrometer Sterivex filter) into a polypropylene conical tube; stored at 4 degC until analysis. Samples were diluted before analysis. All samples were allowed to reach room temperature before analysis. The dilution factors both OCN and SOC samples changed across sediment sampling locations. Samples associated with dry sediment  were diluted with 1 milliliter sample pipetted into analysis vial and diluted with MilliQ water to reach 7 milliliters total. Samples associated with wet sediment samples were diluted with 3.5 milliliter sample pipetted into analysis vial and diluted with MilliQ water to reach 7 milliliters total.

Method_Description: Samples with "OCN" or "SOC" in the name: Manually checked data and calibration curves prior to uploading data. Raw data was processed through a data evaluation script that flagged samples below limit of detection and outside of the standard curve. The coefficient of variation (CV) was calculated among replicates; samples were flagged if CV was outside a given threshold. The flags indicate the limits of detection and CV where applicable. SOC samples were normalized to milligram per kilogram values using the dry mass of the sediment, extraction volume or incubation volume, and water mass in the sediment.
Non-purgeable organic carbon coefficient of variation (CV) was higher than the set threshold. Replicate was removed from summary for being an outlier.
